subject.title: Rename i18n locale codes from region-based (zh-CN/zh-TW) to script-based (zh-Hans/zh-Hant)

question: Should OpenClaw make `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` the canonical Chinese locale identifiers, and if so should `zh-CN`/`zh-TW` remain accepted as migration aliases for existing UI and CLI users?
rationale: The current identifiers are shipped and persisted/user-facing in both Control UI and CLI wizard locale selection, so automation should not choose the breaking-vs-alias compatibility policy on its own.

options.title: Adopt script IDs with migration aliases
options.body: Rename canonical IDs to `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant` while migrating saved Control UI preferences and accepting old CLI/env values through an explicit compatibility path.

options.title: Keep region IDs as the public contract
options.body: Leave `zh-CN`/`zh-TW` as canonical shipped identifiers and document that terminology/script accuracy is handled in locale content rather than ID names.

options.title: Defer until i18n roadmap work
options.body: Keep this issue open but require a broader i18n owner plan before changing docs, UI, CLI, and persisted preferences together.

recommendation.title: Adopt script IDs with migration aliases
recommendation.body: Rename canonical IDs to `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant` while migrating saved Control UI preferences and accepting old CLI/env values through an explicit compatibility path.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged CLI wizard i18n feature is the newest broad locale-selection surface and would need to stay compatible with any canonical-ID change.
